QUALIFICATION TYPES
Programme Description
PLP: PreVocational
Learning
Programme
One-year foundational course to prepare students for
further study at a TVET college. Aimed at school-leavers
with Grade 9, who did not meet entry criteria for a
specific course in NC(V) Level 2.
National
Certificate
Vocational NC(V)
NC(V) programmes integrate theory and practice to
provide students with a broad range of knowledge
and practical skills within specific industry fields. NC(V)
offers learners a vocational alternative to an academic
Grade 10-12, by offering specialised training on NQF
Levels 2-4. After successfully completing NC(V) Level 4,
students can enter the workplace or articulate to Higher
Education.

NATED / Report
191: Engineering
Programmes
Electrical and Mechanical Engineering National
Certificate Programmes range from N4-N6.
Each N Level is delivered over 10 weeks.

NATED / Report 191 / Post Matric programmes consist
of 18 months’ theoretical studies and 18 months’
relevant practical application in the workplace.
Higher
Certificate
Programmes
Higher Certificate Programmes are predominantly
vocational. This means that the course material is
industry-oriented and skills application-based.
Occupational
Certificate
Credit-bearing certificates that range from 1-4 years
in duration. Consists of Engineering and Utilities
programmes which prepare students for a specific trade
where a demand for skilled workers is needed.

HOW TO APPLY .
All applications are done online
via the College website.
You will be required to register an online profile.
Complete the Online Application Form.
Log in with your unique AP Number and Password, which will
sent to your email upon profile registration.
All completed applications are reviewed by a Selection Committee.
Once you have completed your online application, you will receive an
email/sms notification, with your AP number and password.
You can track your application process with your AP number, via the
application portal.
Upload the following certified documents:
Identity Document
Latest Academic Results
Proof of Address
All new applicants must complete the Career Interest
Questionnaire before applying.
Read and accept the POPIA clause.

WORK INTEGRATED
LEARNING (WIL)
The WIL Department provides assistance to full-time students who demonstrate
academic merit and need practical, workplace-based experience to fulfill their

diploma requirements. Graduates can also avail themselves of further
internship and employment prospects.
Email
wil@falsebay.org.za
Exit-Level students must register with the WIL
Department for placement support.
WhatsApp
078 225 8845
The WIL department offers the
following expert support to False Bay
TVET College students:
• Preparing you for the world of
work, through our Work-Readiness
Programmes.
• Assisting you in seeking
workplace-based experience
opportunities in order to obtain

your National N Diploma, National
Certificate, Trade Certificate or
Occupational Certificate.
• Connecting you to employment
and further study opportunities.
• Should you find your own
placement opportunity, the WIL
Department will assist you in
ensuring that the internship is
relevant to your field of study.
• Monitoring and evaluation of
placed students.

The National Student Financial Aid Scheme is a South African
government student financial aid scheme which provides financial
aid to needy students to help pay for the cost of their tertiary
education.
WHAT DOES THE NSFAS BURSARY COVER?
 Study Fees
 Personal Care Allowance
HOW DO I QUALIFY?
 Be a South African Citizen
 Combined household income must not be more than R 350 000
 Be accepted and registered to study at False Bay TVET College
AFTER YOUR STUDY FUNDING IS CONFIRMED, YOU MAY ALSO RECEIVE
ALLOWANCES FOR:
Apply for a NSFAS Bursary online via www.mynsfas.org.za.
Create a myNSFAS account to complete your application.

Ignite, Launch, Build your business with us.
